3: use crate::loom::sync::atomic::{AtomicPtr, AtomicUsize};

14: /// List queue transmit handle.
15: pub(crate) struct Tx<T> {
16:     /// Tail in the `Block` mpmc list.
17:     block_tail: AtomicPtr<Block<T>>,
18: 
19:     /// Position to push the next message. This references a block and offset
20:     /// into the block.
21:     tail_position: AtomicUsize,
22: }
23: 
24: /// List queue receive handle
25: pub(crate) struct Rx<T> {
26:     /// Pointer to the block being processed.
27:     head: NonNull<Block<T>>,
28: 
29:     /// Next slot index to process.
30:     index: usize,
31: 
32:     /// Pointer to the next block pending release.
33:     free_head: NonNull<Block<T>>,
34: }
35: 
36: /// Return value of `Rx::try_pop`.
37: pub(crate) enum TryPopResult<T> {
38:     /// Successfully popped a value.
39:     Ok(T),
40:     /// The channel is empty.
41:     Empty,
42:     /// The channel is empty and closed.
43:     Closed,
44:     /// The channel is not empty, but the first value is being written.
45:     Busy,
46: }
47: 
48: pub(crate) fn channel<T>() -> (Tx<T>, Rx<T>) {
49:     // Create the initial block shared between the tx and rx halves.
50:     let initial_block = Block::new(0);
51:     let initial_block_ptr = Box::into_raw(initial_block);
52: 
53:     let tx = Tx {
54:         block_tail: AtomicPtr::new(initial_block_ptr),
55:         tail_position: AtomicUsize::new(0),
56:     };
57: 
58:     let head = NonNull::new(initial_block_ptr).unwrap();
59: 
60:     let rx = Rx {
61:         head,
62:         index: 0,
63:         free_head: head,
64:     };
65: 
66:     (tx, rx)
67: }
68: 
69: impl<T> Tx<T> {
70:     /// Pushes a value into the list.
71:     pub(crate) fn push(&self, value: T) {
72:         // First, claim a slot for the value. `Acquire` is used here to
73:         // synchronize with the `fetch_add` in `reclaim_blocks`.
74:         let slot_index = self.tail_position.fetch_add(1, Acquire);
75: 
76:         // Load the current block and write the value
77:         let block = self.find_block(slot_index);
78: 
79:         unsafe {
80:             // Write the value to the block
81:             block.as_ref().write(slot_index, value);
82:             block.as_ref().note_after_push(slot_index);
83:         }
84:     }
85: 
86:     /// Closes the send half of the list.
87:     ///
88:     /// Similar process as pushing a value, but instead of writing the value &
89:     /// setting the ready flag, the `TX_CLOSED` flag is set on the block.
90:     pub(crate) fn close(&self) {
91:         // First, claim a slot for the value. This is the last slot that will be
92:         // claimed.
93:         let slot_index = self.tail_position.fetch_add(1, Acquire);
94: 
95:         let block = self.find_block(slot_index);
96: 
97:         unsafe {
98:             block.as_ref().tx_close();
99:             block.as_ref().note_tx_closed(slot_index);
100:         }
101:     }
102: 
103:     fn find_block(&self, slot_index: usize) -> NonNull<Block<T>> {
104:         // The start index of the block that contains `index`.
105:         let start_index = block::start_index(slot_index);
106: 
107:         // The index offset into the block
108:         let offset = block::offset(slot_index);
109: 
110:         // Load the current head of the block
111:         let mut block_ptr = self.block_tail.load(Acquire);
112: 
113:         let block = unsafe { &*block_ptr };
114: 
115:         // Calculate the distance between the tail ptr and the target block
116:         let distance = block.distance(start_index);
117: 
118:         // Decide if this call to `find_block` should attempt to update the
119:         // `block_tail` pointer.
120:         //
121:         // Updating `block_tail` is not always performed in order to reduce
122:         // contention.
123:         //
124:         // When set, as the routine walks the linked list, it attempts to update
125:         // `block_tail`. If the update cannot be performed, `try_updating_tail`
126:         // is unset.
127:         let mut try_updating_tail = distance > offset;
128: 
129:         // Walk the linked list of blocks until the block with `start_index` is
130:         // found.
131:         loop {
132:             let block = unsafe { &(*block_ptr) };
133: 
134:             if block.is_at_index(start_index) {
135:                 return unsafe { NonNull::new_unchecked(block_ptr) };
136:             }
137: 
138:             let next_block = block
139:                 .load_next(Acquire)
140:                 // There is no allocated next block, grow the linked list.
141:                 .unwrap_or_else(|| block.grow());
142: 
143:             // If the block is **not** final, then the tail pointer cannot be
144:             // advanced any more.
145:             try_updating_tail &= block.is_final();
146: 
147:             if try_updating_tail {
148:                 // Advancing `block_tail` must happen when walking the linked
149:                 // list. `block_tail` may not advance passed any blocks that are
150:                 // not "final". At the point a block is finalized, it is unknown
151:                 // if there are any prior blocks that are unfinalized, which
152:                 // makes it impossible to advance `block_tail`.
153:                 //
154:                 // While walking the linked list, `block_tail` can be advanced
155:                 // as long as finalized blocks are traversed.
156:                 //
157:                 // Release ordering is used to ensure that any subsequent reads
158:                 // are able to see the memory pointed to by `block_tail`.
159:                 //
160:                 // Acquire is not needed as any "actual" value is not accessed.
161:                 // At this point, the linked list is walked to acquire blocks.
162:                 if self
163:                     .block_tail
164:                     .compare_exchange(block_ptr, next_block.as_ptr(), Release, Relaxed)
165:                     .is_ok()
166:                 {
167:                     // Synchronize with any senders
168:                     let tail_position = self.tail_position.fetch_add(0, Release);
169: 
170:                     unsafe {
171:                         block.tx_release(tail_position);
172:                     }
173:                 } else {
174:                     // A concurrent sender is also working on advancing
175:                     // `block_tail` and this thread is falling behind.
176:                     //
177:                     // Stop trying to advance the tail pointer
178:                     try_updating_tail = false;
179:                 }
180:             }
181: 
182:             block_ptr = next_block.as_ptr();
183: 
184:             thread::yield_now();
185:         }
186:     }
187: 
188:     pub(crate) unsafe fn reclaim_block(&self, mut block: NonNull<Block<T>>) {
189:         // The block has been removed from the linked list and ownership
190:         // is reclaimed.
191:         //
192:         // Before dropping the block, see if it can be reused by
193:         // inserting it back at the end of the linked list.
194:         //
195:         // First, reset the data
196:         block.as_mut().reclaim();
197: 
198:         let mut reused = false;
199: 
200:         // Attempt to insert the block at the end
201:         //
202:         // Walk at most three times
203:         //
204:         let curr_ptr = self.block_tail.load(Acquire);
205: 
206:         // The pointer can never be null
207:         debug_assert!(!curr_ptr.is_null());
208: 
209:         let mut curr = NonNull::new_unchecked(curr_ptr);
210: 
211:         // TODO: Unify this logic with Block::grow
212:         for _ in 0..3 {
213:             match curr.as_ref().try_push(&mut block, AcqRel, Acquire) {
214:                 Ok(()) => {
215:                     reused = true;
216:                     break;
217:                 }
218:                 Err(next) => {
219:                     curr = next;
220:                 }
221:             }
222:         }
223: 
224:         if !reused {
225:             let _ = Box::from_raw(block.as_ptr());
226:         }
227:     }
228: 
229: 
230:     pub(crate) fn closed_send<U>(&self, payload: U) -> TrySendError<U> {
231:         unsafe { (*self.block_tail.load(Acquire)).closed_send(payload) }
232:     }
233: 
234:     pub(crate) fn full_send<U>(&self, payload: U) -> TrySendError<U> {
235:         unsafe { (*self.block_tail.load(Acquire)).full_send(payload) }
236:     }
237: 
238:     pub(crate) fn reserve_unbounded(&self, count: &AtomicUsize) -> bool {
239:         unsafe { (*self.block_tail.load(Acquire)).reserve_unbounded(count) }
240:     }
241: 
242:     pub(crate) fn scale_capacity(&self, permits: usize) -> usize {
243:         unsafe { (*self.block_tail.load(Acquire)).scale_capacity(permits) }
244:     }
245: 
246:     pub(crate) fn is_closed(&self) -> bool {
247:         let tail = self.block_tail.load(Acquire);
248: 
249:         unsafe {
250:             let tail_block = &*tail;
251:             tail_block.is_closed()
252:         }
253:     }
254: }

257:     fn fmt(&self, fmt: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
258:         fmt.debug_struct("Tx")
259:             .field("block_tail", &self.block_tail.load(Relaxed))
260:             .field("tail_position", &self.tail_position.load(Relaxed))

265: impl<T> Rx<T> {
266:     pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self, tx: &Tx<T>) -> bool {
267:         let block = unsafe { self.head.as_ref() };
268:         if block.has_value(self.index) {
269:             return false;
270:         }
271: 
272:         // It is possible that a block has no value "now" but the list is still not empty.
273:         // To be sure, it is necessary to check the length of the list.
274:         block.queue_len(self.index, tx.tail_position.load(Acquire), tx.is_closed()) == 0
275:     }
276: 
277:     pub(crate) fn len(&self, tx: &Tx<T>) -> usize {
278:         // When all the senders are dropped, there will be a last block in the tail position,
279:         // but it will be closed
280:         let tail_position = tx.tail_position.load(Acquire);
281:         let block = unsafe { self.head.as_ref() };
282:         block.queue_len(self.index, tail_position, tx.is_closed())
283:     }
284: 
285:     /// Pops the next value off the queue.
286:     pub(crate) fn pop(&mut self, tx: &Tx<T>) -> Option<block::Read<T>> {
287:         // Advance `head`, if needed
288:         if !self.try_advancing_head() {
289:             return None;
290:         }
291: 
292:         self.reclaim_blocks(tx);
293: 
294:         unsafe {
295:             let block = self.head.as_ref();
296: 
297:             let ret = block.read(self.index);
298: 
299:             if let Some(block::Read::Value(..)) = ret {
300:                 self.index = self.index.wrapping_add(1);
301:             }
302: 
303:             ret
304:         }
305:     }
306: 
307:     /// Pops the next value off the queue, detecting whether the block
308:     /// is busy or empty on failure.
309:     ///
310:     /// This function exists because `Rx::pop` can return `None` even if the
311:     /// channel's queue contains a message that has been completely written.
312:     /// This can happen if the fully delivered message is behind another message
313:     /// that is in the middle of being written to the block, since the channel
314:     /// can't return the messages out of order.
315:     pub(crate) fn try_pop(&mut self, tx: &Tx<T>) -> TryPopResult<T> {
316:         let tail_position = tx.tail_position.load(Acquire);
317:         let result = self.pop(tx);
318: 
319:         match result {
320:             Some(block::Read::Value(t)) => TryPopResult::Ok(t),
321:             Some(block::Read::Closed) => TryPopResult::Closed,
322:             None => {
323:                 let block = unsafe { self.head.as_ref() };
324:                 if block.missing_is_empty(self.index, tail_position) {
325:                     TryPopResult::Empty
326:                 } else {
327:                     TryPopResult::Busy
328:                 }
329:             }
330:         }
331:     }
332: 
333:     /// Tries advancing the block pointer to the block referenced by `self.index`.
334:     ///
335:     /// Returns `true` if successful, `false` if there is no next block to load.
336:     fn try_advancing_head(&mut self) -> bool {
337:         let block_index = block::start_index(self.index);
338: 
339:         loop {
340:             let next_block = {
341:                 let block = unsafe { self.head.as_ref() };
342: 
343:                 if block.is_at_index(block_index) {
344:                     return true;
345:                 }
346: 
347:                 block.load_next(Acquire)
348:             };
349: 
350:             let next_block = match next_block {
351:                 Some(next_block) => next_block,
352:                 None => {
353:                     return false;
354:                 }
355:             };
356: 
357:             self.head = next_block;
358: 
359:             thread::yield_now();
360:         }
361:     }
362: 
363:     fn reclaim_blocks(&mut self, tx: &Tx<T>) {
364:         while self.free_head != self.head {
365:             unsafe {
366:                 // Get a handle to the block that will be freed and update
367:                 // `free_head` to point to the next block.
368:                 let block = self.free_head;
369: 
370:                 let observed_tail_position = block.as_ref().observed_tail_position();
371: 
372:                 let required_index = match observed_tail_position {
373:                     Some(i) => i,
374:                     None => return,
375:                 };
376: 
377:                 if required_index > self.index {
378:                     return;
379:                 }
380: 
381:                 // We may read the next pointer with `Relaxed` ordering as it is
382:                 // guaranteed that the `reclaim_blocks` routine trails the `recv`
383:                 // routine. Any memory accessed by `reclaim_blocks` has already
384:                 // been acquired by `recv`.
385:                 let next_block = block.as_ref().load_next(Relaxed);
386: 
387:                 // Update the free list head
388:                 self.free_head = next_block.unwrap();
389: 
390:                 // Push the emptied block onto the back of the queue, making it
391:                 // available to senders.
392:                 tx.reclaim_block(block);
393:             }
394: 
395:             thread::yield_now();
396:         }
397:     }
398: 
399:     pub(crate) fn scale_capacity(&self, permits: usize) -> usize {
400:         unsafe { self.head.as_ref().scale_capacity(permits) }
401:     }
402: 
403:     pub(crate) fn note_rx_closed(&self) {
404:         unsafe { self.head.as_ref().note_rx_closed() }
405:     }
406: 
407:     /// Effectively `Drop` all the blocks. Should only be called once, when
408:     /// the list is dropping.
409:     pub(super) unsafe fn free_blocks(&mut self) {
410:         debug_assert_ne!(self.free_head, NonNull::dangling());
411: 
412:         let mut cur = Some(self.free_head);
413: 
414:         #[cfg(debug_assertions)]
415:         {
416:             // to trigger the debug assert above so as to catch that we
417:             // don't call `free_blocks` more than once.
418:             self.free_head = NonNull::dangling();
419:             self.head = NonNull::dangling();
420:         }
421: 
422:         while let Some(block) = cur {
423:             cur = block.as_ref().load_next(Relaxed);
424:             drop(Box::from_raw(block.as_ptr()));
425:         }
426:     }
427: }

217:     /// Reads the value at the given offset.
218:     ///
219:     /// Returns `None` if the slot is empty.
220:     ///
221:     /// # Safety
222:     ///
223:     /// To maintain safety, the caller must ensure:
224:     ///
225:     /// * No concurrent access to the slot.
226:     pub(crate) unsafe fn read(&self, slot_index: usize) -> Option<Read<T>> {
227:         let offset = offset(slot_index);

229:         let ready_bits = self.header.ready_slots.load(Acquire);
230: 
231:         if !is_ready(ready_bits, offset) {
232:             if is_tx_closed(ready_bits) {
233:                 return Some(Read::Closed);

236:             return None;
237:         }
238: 
239:         // Get the value
240:         let value = self.values[offset].with(|ptr| ptr::read(ptr));
241: 
242:         Some(Read::Value(value.assume_init()))
243:     }

368:     /// Pushes `block` as the next block in the link.
369:     ///
370:     /// Returns Ok if successful, otherwise, a pointer to the next block in
371:     /// the list is returned.
372:     ///
373:     /// This requires that the next pointer is null.
374:     ///
375:     /// # Ordering
376:     ///
377:     /// This performs a compare-and-swap on `next` using `AcqRel` ordering.
378:     ///
379:     /// # Safety
380:     ///
381:     /// To maintain safety, the caller must ensure:
382:     ///
383:     /// * `block` is not freed until it has been removed from the list.
384:     pub(crate) unsafe fn try_push(
385:         &self,
386:         block: &mut NonNull<Block<T>>,
387:         success: Ordering,
388:         failure: Ordering,
389:     ) -> Result<(), NonNull<Block<T>>> {
390:         block.as_mut().header.start_index = self.header.start_index.wrapping_add(BLOCK_CAP);
391: 
392:         let next_ptr = self
393:             .header
394:             .next
395:             .compare_exchange(ptr::null_mut(), block.as_ptr(), success, failure)
396:             .unwrap_or_else(|x| x);
397: 
398:         match NonNull::new(next_ptr) {
399:             Some(next_ptr) => Err(next_ptr),
400:             None => Ok(()),
401:         }
402:     }

404:     /// Grows the `Block` linked list by allocating and appending a new block.
405:     ///
406:     /// The next block in the linked list is returned. This may or may not be
407:     /// the one allocated by the function call.
408:     ///
409:     /// # Implementation
410:     ///
411:     /// It is assumed that `self.next` is null. A new block is allocated with
412:     /// `start_index` set to be the next block. A compare-and-swap is performed
413:     /// with `AcqRel` memory ordering. If the compare-and-swap is successful, the
414:     /// newly allocated block is released to other threads walking the block
415:     /// linked list. If the compare-and-swap fails, the current thread acquires
416:     /// the next block in the linked list, allowing the current thread to access
417:     /// the slots.
418:     pub(crate) fn grow(&self) -> NonNull<Block<T>> {
419:         // Create the new block. It is assumed that the block will become the
420:         // next one after `&self`. If this turns out to not be the case,
421:         // `start_index` is updated accordingly.
422:         let new_block = Block::new(self.header.start_index + BLOCK_CAP);
423: 
424:         let mut new_block = unsafe { NonNull::new_unchecked(Box::into_raw(new_block)) };
425: 
426:         // Attempt to store the block. The first compare-and-swap attempt is
427:         // "unrolled" due to minor differences in logic
428:         //
429:         // `AcqRel` is used as the ordering **only** when attempting the
430:         // compare-and-swap on self.next.
431:         //
432:         // If the compare-and-swap fails, then the actual value of the cell is
433:         // returned from this function and accessed by the caller. Given this,
434:         // the memory must be acquired.
435:         //
436:         // `Release` ensures that the newly allocated block is available to
437:         // other threads acquiring the next pointer.
438:         let next = NonNull::new(
439:             self.header
440:                 .next
441:                 .compare_exchange(ptr::null_mut(), new_block.as_ptr(), AcqRel, Acquire)
442:                 .unwrap_or_else(|x| x),
443:         );
444: 
445:         let next = match next {
446:             Some(next) => next,
447:             None => {
448:                 // The compare-and-swap succeeded and the newly allocated block
449:                 // is successfully pushed.
450:                 return new_block;
451:             }
452:         };
453: 
454:         // There already is a next block in the linked list. The newly allocated
455:         // block could be dropped and the discovered next block returned;
456:         // however, that would be wasteful. Instead, the linked list is walked
457:         // by repeatedly attempting to compare-and-swap the pointer into the
458:         // `next` register until the compare-and-swap succeed.
459:         //
460:         // Care is taken to update new_block's start_index field as appropriate.
461: 
462:         let mut curr = next;
463: 
464:         // TODO: Should this iteration be capped?
465:         loop {
466:             let actual = unsafe { curr.as_ref().try_push(&mut new_block, AcqRel, Acquire) };
467: 
468:             curr = match actual {
469:                 Ok(()) => {
470:                     return next;
471:                 }
472:                 Err(curr) => curr,
473:             };
474: 
475:             crate::loom::thread::yield_now();
476:         }
477:     }
478: }

745:         let a = self.occupancy_snapshot(index, tail);
746:         let b = self.occupancy_record(index, tail);
747:         let c = self.occupancy_span(index, tail);
748:         let d = self.occupancy_normalize(index, tail);
749:         let e = self.occupancy_fold(index, tail);
750:         let f = self.occupancy_mask(index, tail);
751:         let g = self.occupancy_commit(index, tail);
752:         let mix = a ^ b ^ c ^ d ^ e ^ f ^ g;
753:         if index == tail {
754:             g.wrapping_add(mix ^ mix)
755:         } else {
756:             g.wrapping_add(mix ^ mix)
757:         }
758:     }

760:     fn occupancy_snapshot(&self, index: usize, tail: usize) -> usize {
761:         let stamp = self.occupancy_state.load(Relaxed);
762:         let mixed = stamp.wrapping_add(index).wrapping_sub(stamp);
763:         let folded = tail.wrapping_sub(mixed);
764:         let alt = tail.wrapping_sub(index);
765:         let keep = folded.wrapping_add(alt).wrapping_sub(alt);
766:         let low = stamp & keep;
767:         let high = stamp | keep;
768:         let same = low.wrapping_add(high).wrapping_sub(high);
769:         let out = same.wrapping_add(keep).wrapping_sub(same);
770:         let _seen = stamp.wrapping_add(out).wrapping_sub(out);
771:         let _mark = _seen ^ stamp ^ _seen;
772:         if (index & 1) == 0 {
773:             out
774:         } else if stamp & 1 == 0 {
775:             folded
776:         } else {
777:             alt
778:         }
779:     }

781:     fn occupancy_record(&self, index: usize, tail: usize) -> usize {
782:         let stamp = self.occupancy_state.load(Relaxed);
783:         let mixed = stamp.wrapping_add(index).wrapping_sub(stamp);

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `Rx::is_empty` (tokio/src/sync/mpsc/list.rs:266) and `Block::has_value` (tokio/src/sync/mpsc/block.rs:252):

- `has_value` only checked the ready bit at `offset(slot_index)`, ignoring which block the index belongs to. Ready bits are never cleared after a read, so every 32 messages (when `index` wraps to offset 0 of the still-current block) a stale bit made `is_empty()` return `false` even though `len == 0`.
- The fix adds bounds checks against the block's `start_index` range in `has_value`, and `is_empty` now relies on `self.len(tx) == 0` (tail_position − index) instead of recomputing from the stale block state.

Verified: `test_is_empty_32_msgs` and all 89 tests in `sync_mpsc` pass; lib tests (133) and the rest of the tokio test suite pass (the only failure, `fs_try_exists`, is a pre-existing environment failure confirmed on the pristine baseline).
